This file documents the conventions resource at the shell, one section per command. Every command is a subcommand of =conventions=, and every section exports its own script into =projects/ores.shell/scripts/library/=. Loading a script runs that one command, so a failure names the command it came from.

** =list=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 6410E6FD-A027-5251-A5E6-914B5BE60CFE
:END:

Reads one page of the collection. Nothing addresses it but the caller's tenant, so it is the read that shows what exists.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example

#+end_example

It is addressed at =refdata.v1.conventions.list=.

#+name: conventions-list

#+end_src

** =get=

** =add=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 58BB584A-FDE2-5882-9079-20F70641BDB5
:END:

Writes a row. The change states that the row must not exist, so a create that collides with an existing row is refused rather than replacing it. The change carries a reason and a commentary, which the server records on it so the row's history says why it moved.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
conventions add <kind_code> <name> <oresmd_uri> <reason> <commentary>
#+end_example

It is addressed at =refdata.v1.conventions.put=.

#+name: conventions-add
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle conventions-add.ores :exports none
conventions add __none__ - - system.new_record generated_script
#+end_src

** =set=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 91E3544A-6F3B-5FDA-94F3-9502836103E0
:END:

Writes a row. The change states no precondition, so it replaces whatever row the key already addresses. The change carries a reason and a commentary, which the server records on it so the row's history says why it moved. Passing --version makes the write conditional on the version the caller last read.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
conventions set <id> <kind_code> <name> <oresmd_uri> <reason> <commentary> [--version <n>]
#+end_example

It is addressed at =refdata.v1.conventions.put=.
